abstract_summary: Organizing long-term memory for multimodal agents remains challenging because existing methods either suffer from expensive question-agnostic offline summaries or naive embedding similarity matching that introduces incomplete and redundant context. To address these issues, we propose GraphMemix, a combinatorial-opti...
citation: GraphMemix: Query-Aware Evidence Forests for Long-Term Multimodal Agent Memory. Geng Li, Yuhao Wang, Dong Li, Jianye Hao, Yuxin Peng. 2026-08-27. https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26983

after the question arrives. Fundamentally,GraphMemixformulates memory selection as query-
conditioned evidence-forest optimization: nodes capture the direct utility of individual memories,
while edges capture their incremental value when conditioned on an anchor. To instantiate this ob-
jective,GraphMemixstarts from multi-view matching anchors and expands through schema and
semantic edges to reconstruct a bounded, query-relevant candidate subgraph. A node verifier esti-
matesdirectsupport,whileanEvidence-ChainVerifierestimateswhethereachanchor-conditioned
relation contributes complementary information rather than redundancy or conflict. The resulting
objective jointly selects relevant memories and reliable relations, recovering low-similarity con-
text while suppressing uncertain expansion. For any fixed node set, its optimal maximum-weight
forest is obtained

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The GPT-5-mini judge is validated by a 97.0% agreement audit against manual inspection of 200 stratified answers, and the reported gains are corroborated by benchmark-native metrics across four datasets.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are reported as downstream QA accuracy judged by an external GPT-5-mini evaluator, with benchmark-native ground-truth metrics (EM, MCQ EM, lexical Recall) reported alongside.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system is optimized through a combinatorial forest objective whose node utilities and edge costs are produced by frozen LVLM verifiers (node verifier and Evidence-Chain Verifier) fused with fixed embedding similarity priors.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical gains (+11.75 to +12.33 Judge Accuracy macro-averages) and native metric improvements directly support the core claims of superior accuracy and a favorable lifecycle-efficiency Pareto frontier.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation spans four diverse long-term multimodal memory benchmarks (ATM-Bench, Mem-Gallery, MemEye, H2HMem) using multiple reader backbones (Qwen3-VL and Gemma 4) against five recognized baselines, reporting both LLM judge accuracy and benchmark-native metrics alongside ablations and lifecycle runtime analyses.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance improvements are corroborated by standard benchmark-native ground-truth metrics (Normalized EM, MCQ EM, lexical recall) as well as a 97% human agreement audit on GPT-5-mini judgments.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Downstream QA evaluation assessed using external benchmark metrics (EM, MCQ EM, lexical Recall) and an external LLM judge (GPT-5-mini) across four independent datasets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Combinatorial optimization combining fixed multimodal embedding similarity priors with prompting-based node and edge-chain verification scoring from frozen LVLMs (Qwen3-VL-8B or Gemma-4-12B).

primary.limitations: The manuscript notes boundary conditions regarding dependence on bounded candidate graph recall, reliance on prompt-following structured JSON generation for verifiers, and fixed budget constraints.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying multi-view candidate expansion, explicit listwise node scoring, anchor-conditioned edge verification, and a two-stage solver combining 1-swap search with exact Kruskal forest recomputation under fixed hyperparameters.
primary.quality_rationale: GraphMemix provides a rigorous, self-contained formulation solving clear limitations of existing multimodal RAG and offline memory summarization methods, validated comprehensively across diverse datasets and metrics with appropriate controls and ablations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces GraphMemix, a test-time graph optimization framework that structures multimodal agent memory retrieval as query-aware evidence-forest selection, balancing direct relevance against relational complementarity while bounding full-lifecycle computation.

scholarly_quality.rationale: GraphMemix provides a rigorous, self-contained formulation solving clear limitations of existing multimodal RAG and offline memory summarization methods, validated comprehensively across diverse datasets and metrics with appropriate controls and ablations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The manuscript notes boundary conditions regarding dependence on bounded candidate graph recall, reliance on prompt-following structured JSON generation for verifiers, and fixed budget constraints.
